decision: Rejected for production. Retain the existing automatic controller and steady pacing gain 1.1. This file records an isolated diagnostic, not an available setting or shipped feature.

source.source_mode: immutable archive plus isolated prototype.patch; never installed in production

additional_observation_trial.purpose: Collect the existing controller event stream throughout another prototype policer run; throughput excluded from comparisons because observation adds CPU work.
additional_observation_trial.note: Separate diagnostic trial; event collection adds CPU work and its throughput is not used as comparative evidence.

experimental_state_machine: Collect only in steady probe, outside RTT calibration/candidates, without spurious-loss increases or long send inactivity. Do not equate low bytes-in-flight with low application demand.

Require at least 1second, 2000 acknowledged packets, 16 lost packets, and loss in two distinct 250ms intervals. These are experimental sample gates, not a statistically reliable policer classification.

Temporarily set effective gain 1.0 and cap the target at entry pacing divided by 1.1, preventing a rising estimate from canceling the intervention. Ignore the first max(100 ms, 2 RTT) when evaluating it.

Explore for at most 2seconds after settling. Require enough samples, ACKed byte rate at least 95% of baseline, and normalized loss at most 60% of baseline before a temporary hold lasting at most 3seconds. Always remove the cap at its deadline, even without ACK callbacks, then allow at least 1second without the cap.
Clear on idle, path/queue ambiguity or increased spurious loss. The experiment does not identify an ISP policy and never runs in Startup.

unit_validation.command: go test -race ./internal/congestion ./internal/ackhandler in the isolated patched quic-go module
coverage: hard cap survives an inflated bandwidth estimate
deadline removes cap without ACK callbacks
Startup/RTT grace/queue/one ACK batch/sparse loss do not arm
low flight relative to cwnd is not mistaken for no demand

rejection_reasons: No lasting intervention was observed in the comparative policer telemetry. Throughput differences cannot be attributed to the experiment merely because their means differ.

The low-queue predicate uses max(latest RTT,smoothed RTT) on every ACK. Every invalid observation postpones eligibility by one second, followed by another full evidence window. Isolated timing noise at a high ACK rate can indefinitely starve exploration. Loosening this after seeing the result would require a new, separately validated design.

Comparing target pacing against its entry value is not independent evidence of lower actual wire send rate: the entry cap guarantees that inequality. Causal evaluation needs send-time or wire-byte measurements over matched windows.
A zero-byte congestion event represents ECN but does not directly cancel this experiment's evidence. Explicit congestion handling must be included before reconsidering such a policy.

Selecting a baseline because loss is high biases a subsequent before/after comparison toward apparent improvement. Small packet windows, ACK batching, changing FEC redundancy and application demand add confounding factors; a short random-loss dip must not cause an indefinite cap.
next_research_boundary: Aggregate queue and loss evidence over completed packet rounds or RTT windows, separating path calibration from healthy observations; do not require every individual RTT sample to be noiseless.

Measure actual send and ACK-delivery spans, retain a hard probe deadline, add ECN invalidation, and use an independent confirmation or reversal phase. Keep periodic upward capacity discovery and reset on path changes.

Repeat short/high RTT, ACK aggregation, random and burst loss, different bucket sizes, bandwidth step up/down, and sparse demand before considering production. A fixed global gain decrease is not justified by the current small matrix.
